outcome: adverse effects (transient hypertension, transient hyperglycemia, transient slowing of postnatal weight gain)
cohort: The study included 51 extremely preterm infants (median gestational age 25.7 weeks) with a patent ductus arteriosus and severe respiratory conditions, who were treated with betamethasone around 28 days of life.
finding: Oral betamethasone treatment in extremely preterm infants with severe respiratory conditions was associated with improved weaning from invasive ventilation and patent ductus arteriosus closure, potentially reducing the need for surgical or endovascular interventions for PDA.
followup_time: Observations taken around 28-35 days postnatal age
